newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine floods kill 22, maroon President Ramos.
newsitem.headline: Philippine floods kill 22, maroon President Ramos.

text.p: At least 22 people died as torrential rains battered the Philippines on Monday, flooding thousands of homes, sending people fleeing to rooftops and bringing the capital Manila to a standstill.

President Fidel Ramos was caught in a huge traffic jam after three days of storms unleashed floodwaters as deep as eight feet (1.5 metres) and knocked out power in many areas of the city, including at Manila's international airport, officials said.

Six people drowned when their pleasure boat capsized off the central island of Cebu while 16 were drowned, electrocuted or crushed to death by falling walls and landslides in Manila and nearby towns. "This is the first time this has happened here," an airport official said as water lay ankle-deep on sections of the runway and the power supply room, plunging the terminal building into darkness.

philippine Airlines cancelled its domestic and international flights until midnight. Many international flights were delayed and five others diverted to Mactan airport in the central Philippines because of poor visibility.
Financial markets and government offices in this metropolis of 10 million people closed and private offices sent employees home.
In some towns north of Manila, local officials appealed for helicopters and rubber boats to rescue residents from their homes, disaster coordinating council officer Emma Tabalanza said.

"Many of our residents have to be rescued because the waters are continuing to rise," Mayor Alexander Payumo of Dinalupihan town said. "Some of our people are already on rooftops," Mayor Kate Gordon of Olongapo city, near Dinalupihan, said in a radio broadcast. The virtual collapse of basic services in Manila raised questions about the infrastructure in a country that has billed itself as one of Asia's prime investment destinations, political analysts said.
But Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said he was not worried that investors might be turned off.
"We can't force people to come to the offices. There were floods everywhere," he told Reuters. "Even in New York, if they have a snow storm, the markets are also closed down."
A presidential palace statement said it took Ramos almost two hours to travel 12 km (seven miles) back to the palace from a speaking engagement because of the traffic jam.
The rains marked the end of a long dry season that had left parts of the country short of water.
The rainy season usually begins around May and lasts until November, averaging more than 20 typhoons during the period.
Among those killed in Manila were a father and a son buried in a landslide, three street vendors crushed by a collapsing wall and three men who touched a live wire.
A landslide swallowed four houses in Subic town, killing two residents. Four were still missing, police said. Floods submerged more than 2,500 homes in Bataan province.
The Weather Bureau warned that the rains, the result of an active low pressure system hovering over Luzon island, would continue at least until Tuesday.
